correctness.rationale: For uniform digit a and k highest position, N >= a b^k whereas E_b(N)=r a³<=a(k+1)(b-1)². The inequality b^k>(k+1)(b-1)² for k>=3 excludes all longer forms. k<=2 yields the five exact Diophantine equations with valid 2<=a<b and converses; (a00) impossible since a=b contradiction. Three quadratic cases are norm equations for Pell units, including a complete positive descent for x²-12a²=-3 via inverse (x,a)->(7x-24a,7a-2x), base witnesses 22,313,4366. Main base families b=a² and b=2a²-1 each yield sqrt X and sqrt(X/2); their intersection and remaining Pell families have O(log X) bases. Even bases from square family half sqrt X; others are O(log X). Independent exact digit enumeration for bases 2..300 found 34 uniform fixed points and agreed with Diophantine families; generalized Pell witnesses checked. These finite checks support but do not prove the all-base count.

evidence: For E_b(n) = leading digit times sum of squared base-b digits, all nontrivial uniform-positive-digit fixed points in all integer bases b>=2 are exactly five <=3-digit patterns (a0), (aa), (a0a), (aa0), (aaa) with five displayed quadratic Diophantine equations; base count B(X)=(1+1/sqrt(2))sqrt(X)+O(log X), even-base count 0.5sqrt(X)+O(log X).
value.rationale: Uniform-positive-digit fixed points are a coherent natural restricted class of the newly introduced elated dynamical map, not an arbitrary finite numerical slice. Five-pattern completeness and exact asymptotic base density distinguish abundant square/square-triangular patterns from sparse Pell subfamilies, and exhibit infinitely many even nonsquare bases with nontrivial fixed points, relevant to the motivating universal-elation question.
